subproblems.title: Mass densities are unique
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), x ∈ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) and θ, θ' ∈ ℝ. Suppose HasMassDensity T x θ and HasMassDensity T x θ', i.e. θ ≥ 0, θ' ≥ 0, and the ratio T.massOn(B_ρ(x)) / (ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) ∈ [0, ∞] (ω_n = unitBallVolume n, B_ρ(x) the open ball) tends both to ofReal θ and to ofReal θ' as ρ → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ). Then θ = θ'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (θ θ' : ℝ), HasMassDensity T x θ → HasMassDensity T x θ' → θ = θ'
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("Densities are unique: if HasMassDensity S x θ and HasMassDensity S x θ', the two limits along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 in the Hausdorff space ℝ≥0∞ agree, so ofReal θ = ofReal θ', and θ, θ' ≥ 0 give θ = θ'"), stated for an arbitrary domain U and current T. Simon defines Θ^n(μ_T, x) as a limit (Ch. 7, 7.3.1; contract definition HasMassDensity), so it is unique when it exists.
Notation: f(ρ) := T.massOn(B_ρ(x)) / (unitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^n)) ∈ [0, ∞] for ρ ∈ ℝ. By definition, HasMassDensity T x θ means 0 ≤ θ and f(ρ) → ENNReal.ofReal θ as ρ → 0⁺, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ.
1. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial: each of its members contains an interval (0, ε) with ε > 0, which is nonempty (ℝ is densely ordered without maximum; Mathlib provides the NeBot instance for 𝓝[>] a).
2. [0, ∞] = ℝ≥0∞ with its order topology is a Hausdorff space, and in a Hausdorff space a function has at most one limit along a nontrivial filter (tendsto_nhds_unique). By the two hypotheses, f → ofReal θ and f → ofReal θ' along 𝓝[>] 0. By step 1 the filter is nontrivial, so ofReal θ = ofReal θ'.
3. ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞): for p, q ≥ 0, ofReal p = ofReal q iff p = q (ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff). The first components of the hypotheses give θ ≥ 0 and θ' ≥ 0, so step 2 yields θ = θ'. ∎
proof_key_steps: 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ and ℝ≥0∞ is Hausdorff, so the two density limits coincide: ofReal θ = ofReal θ'.
θ ≥ 0, θ' ≥ 0 and injectivity of ENNReal.ofReal on [0, ∞) give θ = θ'.

subproblems.title: The density equals the multiplicity Hⁿ-a.e. on the carrier
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents S; M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult). Let Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy HasMassDensity S x Θ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then Θ(x) = θ(x) (θ(x) ∈ ℕ cast to ℝ) for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, i.e. for almost every x with respect to μHE[n] restricted to R.carrier.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Θ : Euclid P → ℝ), R.Represents S → (∀ x : Euclid P, HasMassDensity S x (Θ x)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict R.carrier), Θ x = (R.mult x : ℝ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof ("Θ = θ for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M"), together with the remark in step 2 that μ and ν := H^n⌞M have the same null sets inside M. In Simon this is Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) with Theorem 1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298–325), as used in Ch. 4, 3.12 (chapter-04.txt lines 350–354: "Θ^n(V, x) = θ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (by Remark 1.8(2))"). (The parent's citation "Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2)" refers to this remark of Ch. 3.) The pointwise statement of step 3 — approximate tangent planes (α), Besicovitch–Lebesgue points (β) and the computation 3(a)–(b) — is exactly the sibling ae_density_mult (the reused accepted declaration Submission.rsd_ae_hasMassDensity_mult), whose accepted proof carries out that argument. It is used here as a black box.
Notation: M = R.carrier (a Borel set), θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, H^n = μHE[n], ν := H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, and μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity θ, so μ(B) = ∫⁻_B θ dν for Borel B.
1. Apply the sibling ae_density_mult with U := ℝ^P (open), T := S and R; R.Represents S is a hypothesis. It gives HasMassDensity S x θ(x) for μ-a.e. x, with θ(x) cast to ℝ.
2. Let x be such a point. By hypothesis also HasMassDensity S x Θ(x), so the sibling density_unique (U := ℝ^P, T := S) gives Θ(x) = θ(x). Hence Θ(x) = θ(x) for μ-a.e. x, i.e. the set Z := {x : Θ(x) ≠ θ(x)} satisfies μ(Z) = 0 (μ applied to an arbitrary set is its outer measure).
3. ν ≪ μ.
- The function x ↦ θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞] is Borel: θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable (axiom measurable_mult), and every map out of ℕ (discrete σ-algebra) is measurable, in particular the cast ℕ → [0, ∞].
- θ(x) ≥ 1 for every x ∈ M (axiom mult_pos). Since ν is carried by the Borel set M, θ(x) ≠ 0 for ν-a.e. x.
- Let B be Borel with μ(B) = 0. Then ∫⁻_B θ dν = 0, so θ = 0 ν-a.e. on B; as θ ≠ 0 ν-a.e., ν(B) = 0. (This is Mathlib's withDensity_absolutelyContinuous': ν ≪ ν.withDensity θ when θ is ν-a.e. measurable and ν-a.e. nonzero.)
- For an arbitrary set Z with μ(Z) = 0 choose a Borel set B ⊇ Z with μ(B) = 0 (measurable superset of a null set). Then ν(Z) ≤ ν(B) = 0.
4. By steps 2 and 3, ν(Z) = 0. That is, Θ(x) = θ(x) for ν-a.e. x, where ν = μHE[n].restrict R.carrier. This is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: The reused accepted density theorem (sibling ae_density_mult) gives HasMassDensity S x θ(x) for μ_R-a.e. x.
Uniqueness of densities (sibling density_unique) turns this into Θ = θ μ_R-a.e.
Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n⌞M ≪ μ_R = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, so Θ = θ holds H^n⌞M-a.e.

subproblems.title: The density vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. off the carrier (Upper Density Theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents S; M = R.carrier). Let Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy HasMassDensity S x Θ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then H^n({x ∈ ℝ^P : x ∉ M and Θ(x) > 0}) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] (evaluated as an outer measure).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Θ : Euclid P → ℝ), R.Represents S → (∀ x : Euclid P, HasMassDensity S x (Θ x)) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) {x | x ∉ R.carrier ∧ 0 < Θ x} = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("Θ = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∉ M"). In Simon this is the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–722), which is derived from the comparison Theorem 3.3 (line 602) and the 5-times covering Lemma 3.4. The three ingredients of step 4 are reused accepted declarations:
- the Vitali 5r-covering estimate μH[n]_{10δ}(A) ≤ 10^n (tω_n)^{-1} μ(U') (letting δ ↓ 0) is the sibling lower_density_comparison (Submission.dorag_sn_hausdorff_le_mul_of_lower_density);
- "by outer regularity there is an open U' ⊇ A with μ(U') < ε" is the sibling null_open_superset (Submission.dorag_sn_open_superset_measure_lt);
- the identity S.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)) of step 1 (im_mass_measure (a)) is the sibling mass_eq_measure (Submission.rsd_massOn_eq_measure, which states exactly im_mass_measure (a)).
Notation: M = R.carrier (Borel), θ = R.mult, H^n = μHE[n], μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, ω_n := unitBallVolume n = Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n. B_ρ(x) is the open ball and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball.
1. Constants. 0 < ω_n < ∞: the open unit ball of ℝ^n is nonempty, open and bounded, and Lebesgue measure is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on bounded sets. This includes n = 0, where ℝ^0 is a point and ω_0 = 1.
2. Mass equals measure on balls. For every x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ ∈ ℝ, B_ρ(x) is an open subset of ℝ^P. So the sibling mass_eq_measure with U := ℝ^P (open), T := S and W := B_ρ(x) gives S.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)).
3. μ vanishes off M. Since M is Borel, μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = ∫⁻_{ℝ^P∖M} θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫⁻ θ d(H^n⌞((ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M)) = 0, because (ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M = ∅.
4. μ is locally finite. Let x ∈ ℝ^P. The closed ball B̄_1(x) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contained in ℝ^P = U. So μ(B_1(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_1(x)) = ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_1(x)} θ dH^n < ∞ by the axiom locallyIntegrable_mult.
5. Fix k ∈ ℕ and put t := 1/(k+1) > 0 and A := {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > t}. By step 3 and monotonicity, μ(A) ≤ μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0.
6. Lower density bound on A. Put c := t·ω_n, a positive real number by step 1. Let x ∈ A and write f(s) := S.massOn(B_s(x)) / (ω_n · ofReal(s^n)).
- Since HasMassDensity S x Θ(x), f(s) → ofReal Θ(x) as s → 0⁺. As 0 ≤ t < Θ(x), ofReal t < ofReal Θ(x), so (ofReal t, ∞] is a neighbourhood of the limit. Hence there is t₀ > 0 with f(s) > ofReal t for every s ∈ (0, t₀).
- Fix s ∈ (0, t₀). The denominator d := ω_n · ofReal(s^n) satisfies 0 < d < ∞ (step 1 and s^n > 0). So ofReal t < S.massOn(B_s(x))/d gives ofReal t · d ≤ S.massOn(B_s(x)) (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le).
- Since t, ω_n and s^n are nonnegative and ω_n < ∞, ofReal t · d = ofReal(t · ω_n · s^n) = ofReal(c s^n).
- With step 2 and B_s(x) ⊆ B̄_s(x): ofReal(c s^n) ≤ S.massOn(B_s(x)) = μ(B_s(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_s(x)) for all s ∈ (0, t₀).
7. Comparison. The sibling lower_density_comparison with N := P, this n, and c > 0 gives a constant C ∈ [0, ∞) (C ≠ ∞) such that, for the measure ν := μ, every open O ⊇ A satisfies H^n(A) ≤ C · μ(O); its density hypothesis is step 6.
8. Small open neighbourhoods. Let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. By step 5, μ(A) = 0, and by step 4 every x ∈ A has a radius r = 1 with μ(B_r(x)) < ∞. So the sibling null_open_superset gives an open O ⊇ A with μ(O) < ε. By step 7, H^n(A) ≤ C · μ(O) ≤ C · ε.
9. Take ε := 1/j for j ∈ ℕ (in [0, ∞], 1/0 = ∞ > 0 and 1/j > 0 for every j). Since C < ∞, C · (1/j) → C · 0 = 0 as j → ∞ (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul with ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero). Passing to the limit in H^n(A) ≤ C · (1/j) gives H^n(A) ≤ 0, hence H^n(A) = 0.
10. Union over t. If x ∉ M and Θ(x) > 0, the Archimedean property gives k ∈ ℕ with 1/(k+1) < Θ(x). So {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0} ⊆ ⋃_{k∈ℕ} {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 1/(k+1)}. By step 9 each set in the union is H^n-null, and countable subadditivity together with monotonicity gives H^n({x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0}) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_R vanishes off M, is locally finite, and S.massOn = μ_R on open balls (sibling mass_eq_measure).
On A_t = {x ∉ M : Θ(x) > t} the density hypothesis gives μ_R(B̄_s(x)) ≥ t ω_n s^n for small s.

Vitali comparison (sibling lower_density_comparison) gives H^n(A_t) ≤ C μ_R(O) for every open O ⊇ A_t, and outer regularity at the μ_R-null set A_t (sibling null_open_superset) makes μ_R(O) arbitrarily small, so H^n(A_t) = 0.
A countable union over t = 1/(k+1) gives H^n({x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0}) = 0.

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (R : IMRep univ n with R.Represents S). Let Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy HasMassDensity S x Θ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Then R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M is equal to H^n.withDensity(x ↦ ofReal Θ(x)), where H^n = μHE[n]; equivalently μ_R(A) = ∫⁻_A ofReal Θ dH^n for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P.

Source: step 5 of the parent proof ("By steps 3 and 4 and Θ ≥ 0, ofReal ∘ Θ = θ·1_M H^n-a.e. Therefore for every Borel A, ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n = ∫_{A∩M} θ dH^n = μ(A)"). In Simon this is the canonical representative V = v(M_V, θ_V) with θ_V(x) = Θ^n(V, x) of Ch. 4, 3.12 (chapter-04.txt lines 350–354). Here it holds without stationarity because Θ is assumed to exist at every point.
Notation: M = R.carrier (Borel), θ = R.mult, H^n = μHE[n], μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ, and f(x) := ofReal Θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞]. No measurability of f is assumed or needed: lower integrals ∫⁻ are defined for every function, and a.e.-equal functions have equal lower integrals.
1. Reduction. Two measures on ℝ^P are equal as soon as they agree on all Borel sets (Measure.ext). Fix a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. Left side. μ(A) = ∫⁻_A θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n. This uses withDensity_apply for the Borel set A and (H^n⌞M)⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict).
3. Right side. (H^n.withDensity f)(A) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n (withDensity_apply). Splitting A along the Borel set M, ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ∫⁻_{A∩M} f dH^n + ∫⁻_{A∖M} f dH^n (lintegral_inter_add_sdiff; this is additivity of the restricted measure H^n⌞A = H^n⌞(A∩M) + H^n⌞(A∖M) and holds for every f).
4. The part A ∩ M. By the sibling density_eq_mult, Θ(x) = θ(x) for H^n⌞M-a.e. x. Since A ∩ M ⊆ M, the same holds for H^n⌞(A∩M)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). At such x, f(x) = ofReal θ(x) = θ(x), because ofReal of a natural number is that number in [0, ∞]. Hence ∫⁻_{A∩M} f dH^n = ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n (lintegral_congr_ae).
5. The part A ∖ M.
- Let N := {x : x ∉ M and Θ(x) > 0}; by the sibling null_off_carrier, H^n(N) = 0.
- Let x ∈ A ∖ M with f(x) ≠ 0. Then f(x) > 0, and ofReal p > 0 iff p > 0, so Θ(x) > 0 and x ∈ N. Thus {x : x ∈ A ∖ M and f(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ N is H^n-null; that is, H^n-a.e. x satisfies (x ∈ A ∖ M ⇒ f(x) = 0).
- As A ∖ M is Borel, this means f = 0 for H^n⌞(A∖M)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff'). Hence ∫⁻_{A∖M} f dH^n = ∫⁻_{A∖M} 0 dH^n = 0.
6. Conclusion. By steps 3, 4, 5 and 2, (H^n.withDensity f)(A) = ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n + 0 = μ(A). As A was an arbitrary Borel set, step 1 gives R.measure = μHE[n].withDensity (x ↦ ofReal Θ(x)). ∎

On A ∩ M, ofReal Θ = θ H^n-a.e. (sibling density_eq_mult), giving ∫⁻_{A∩M} θ dH^n = μ_R(A).
On A ∖ M, ofReal Θ = 0 H^n-a.e. (sibling null_off_carrier), so that part vanishes.

subproblems.title: Translation invariance of f·Hⁿ for a translation-invariant density f
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), and y ∈ ℝ^P with f(y + x) = f(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Let ν := H^n.withDensity f, so ν(B) = ∫⁻_B f dH^n for Borel B. Then ν((x ↦ y + x)⁻¹(A)) = ν(A) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P; that is, ν(A − y) = ν(A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (y : Euclid P), (∀ x : Euclid P, f (y + x) = f x) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f ((fun x => y + x) ⁻¹' A) = (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (translation invariance (i)), with the density function ofReal ∘ Θ of the parent replaced by an arbitrary f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] satisfying f(y + ·) = f. The parent's computation μ(A − y) = ∫_{A−y} ofReal Θ dH^n = ∫_A ofReal Θ(x − y) dH^n(x) = ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n is the same change of variables, written here through the preimage form.
Notation: τ(x) := y + x on ℝ^P, H^n = μHE[n], and ν := H^n.withDensity f.
1. τ is a bijective isometry of ℝ^P (|τ(a) − τ(b)| = |a − b|, inverse x ↦ −y + x); in Mathlib it is IsometryEquiv.addLeft y. In particular τ is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding for the Borel σ-algebra (Homeomorph.addLeft y). Since τ is continuous, τ⁻¹(A) is Borel whenever A is.
2. H^n is invariant under bijective isometries: τ_#H^n = H^n, i.e. τ is measure preserving from (ℝ^P, H^n) to (ℝ^P, H^n) (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). The reason is that μHE[n] is a constant multiple of the Hausdorff measure μH[n], which is defined through diameters only.
3. Change of variables. For a measure-preserving measurable embedding τ, every function g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] and every set B ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(B)} g(τ(a)) dH^n(a) = ∫⁻_B g dH^n (MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_preimage_emb; no measurability of g is needed because τ is a measurable embedding). With g := f and B := A this reads ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(A)} f(y + a) dH^n(a) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n.
4. By hypothesis f(y + a) = f(a) for every a ∈ ℝ^P, so the left side of step 3 equals ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(A)} f dH^n.
5. For Borel B, ν(B) = ∫⁻_B f dH^n (withDensity_apply; only measurability of B is needed). Both A and τ⁻¹(A) are Borel by step 1. So ν(τ⁻¹(A)) = ∫⁻_{τ⁻¹(A)} f dH^n = ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ν(A), using steps 3 and 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ y + x is a bijective isometry, hence a measurable embedding that preserves μHE[n].
Change of variables for lower integrals along a measure-preserving embedding, together with f(y + ·) = f, gives ∫⁻_{(y+·)⁻¹A} f dH^n = ∫⁻_A f dH^n, i.e. ν((y+·)⁻¹A) = ν(A).

subproblems.title: n-homogeneity of f·Hⁿ for a dilation-invariant density f
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), and λ > 0 with f(λx) = f(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Let ν := H^n.withDensity f. Then for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P, ν(λA) = λ^n·ν(A), where λA = (x ↦ λx)(A) is the image of A; in [0, ∞] this reads ν(λA) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → (∀ x : Euclid P, f (lam • x) = f x) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f ((fun x => lam • x) '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ n) * (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).withDensity f A

Source: step 7 of the parent proof (homogeneity (ii)), with the density function ofReal ∘ Θ replaced by an arbitrary f satisfying f(λ·) = f. The change of variables ∫_{λA} g dH^n = λ^n ∫_A g(λw) dH^n(w) used there is the sibling dilation_change_of_variables (the reused accepted declaration Submission.euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables, which step 7 cites).
Notation: δ(x) := λx on ℝ^P, H^n = μHE[n], ν := H^n.withDensity f, and D := δ(A) = λA.
1. δ is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse x ↦ λ⁻¹x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ, λ ≠ 0). Hence δ is a measurable embedding and injective. So D = δ(A) is Borel (the image of a Borel set under a measurable embedding), and δ⁻¹(D) = A by injectivity.
2. Apply part (ii) of the sibling dilation_change_of_variables with c := λ > 0, M := D and g := f. It gives ∫⁻_{δ⁻¹(D)} f(λz) dH^n(z) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ∫⁻_D f dH^n; it holds for every f : ℝ^P → [0, ∞].
3. By step 1, δ⁻¹(D) = A, and by hypothesis f(λz) = f(z) for every z. So step 2 becomes ∫⁻_A f dH^n = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ∫⁻_D f dH^n.
4. A and D are Borel, so ν(A) = ∫⁻_A f dH^n and ν(D) = ∫⁻_D f dH^n (withDensity_apply). Hence ν(A) = ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) · ν(D).
5. Multiply both sides by ofReal(λ^n). Since λ^n ≥ 0 and λ⁻¹^n ≥ 0, ofReal(λ^n) · ofReal(λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal(λ^n · λ⁻¹^n) = ofReal((λ · λ⁻¹)^n) = ofReal(1) = 1, using λ ≠ 0. Therefore ofReal(λ^n) · ν(A) = ν(D) = ν(λA). ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ λx is a homeomorphism, so λA is Borel and (λ·)⁻¹(λA) = A.
The reused change of variables (sibling dilation_change_of_variables) with g = f and f(λ·) = f gives ν(A) = λ^{-n} ν(λA).
Multiplying by ofReal(λ^n) gives ν(λA) = ofReal(λ^n)·ν(A).

This simpler accepted declaration is chosen instead because its candidate 591230fd is an ancestor of the candidate 71a35e92 of sibling ae_density_mult, so it adds no Lean code to this node.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–767, printed without proof). It is the identity μ_T(W) = M_W(T) of Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8 (lines 264–282) for T = τ(M, θ, ξ), and it is the identity μ_T(B_ρ(x)) = M_{B_ρ(x)}(T) used in steps 2–4 of the parent proof.

Notation:
- H^n = μHE[n].
- μ := R.measure = θH^n⌞M, a Borel measure on ℝ^P that vanishes outside M ⊆ U and is finite on compact subsets of U (axiom locallyIntegrable_mult).
- For an n-covector α, |α| := (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, summed over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P} (covectorEuclideanNorm). This is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector of α, hence a norm on n-covectors.
- ‖α‖ is the operator norm, and ⟨α, v⟩ := v(α) for an n-vector v.

Replace ξ by a Borel function that agrees with it H^n-a.e. on M. This changes neither the integral formula for T nor any a.e. statement below.

1. Linear algebra. Let τ₁, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, τ_i = Σ_j A_{ij} e_j, and for strictly increasing I let A_I := (A_{i,I(k)})_{i,k}. Expand α(τ₁, …, τ_n) by multilinearity, drop the non-injective index maps (α is alternating), and group the injective ones by their image. This gives α(τ₁, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
(a) By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ₁, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α.
(b) Let J be the linear map sending an n-vector v to the n-covector J(v) with J(v)(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}) = ⟨e^I, v⟩ for strictly increasing I. Here e^I := dx^{I(1)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n)}, so e^I(v₁, …, v_n) = det(⟨e_{I(k)}, v_j⟩)_{k,j}. Suppose ⟨α, v⟩ = ε α(τ₁, …, τ_n) for all α, with ε ∈ {1, −1}. Then ⟨e^I, v⟩ = ε det(A_I), so |J(v)| = (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = 1 and ⟨J(v), v⟩ = ε J(v)(τ₁, …, τ_n) = ε² Σ_I det(A_I)² = 1.
For n = 0 these facts are immediate: α(τ) = α(()) and |α| = |α(())|.
By the axiom orients of R (IsUnitOrientationOf), ξ(x) has this form for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, hence for μ-a.e. x. Therefore, μ-a.e.: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α, and β(x) := J(ξ(x)) satisfies |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1. The map β = J∘ξ is Borel.

2. M_W(T) ≤ μ(W). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. The integrand θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ vanishes off the compact set K := spt ω ⊆ U. By step 1 it is bounded in absolute value by θ1_{M∩K} H^n-a.e. on M, which is integrable. Hence T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ|ω| dH^n ≤ μ(W). The zero form is admissible, so M_W(T) = sup ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(W).

3. Choice of K and V. Let λ be real with 0 ≤ λ < μ(W); it suffices to find an admissible ω with T(ω) > λ.
- The sets W_j := {y ∈ W : |y| < j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) > 1/j} increase to W and have compact closures W̄_j ⊆ W. By continuity from below, μ(K) > λ for K := W̄_j with j large, and μ(K) < ∞ because K is a compact subset of U.
- Fix ε > 0 with μ(K) > λ + 3ε.
- Pick d > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ d} ⊆ W. Since K₁ is compact, μ⌞K₁ is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence outer regular, so there is an open V' ⊇ K with μ(K₁ ∩ V' ∖ K) < ε.
- Put V := V' ∩ {y : dist(y, K) < d}. Then V is open, K ⊆ V, V̄ ⊆ K₁ ⊆ W, and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.

4. A smooth admissible form.
- β is Borel with |β| = 1 μ-a.e., so β ∈ L¹(μ⌞K). Continuous compactly supported maps are dense in L¹ of the finite Borel (hence regular) measure μ⌞K on ℝ^P, so there is a continuous compactly supported g with ∫_K |g − β| dμ < ε.
- Let π(α) := α / max(1, |α|), the nearest-point retraction onto the closed unit ball of the Euclidean norm |·|; π is 1-Lipschitz. Then g₁ := π∘g is continuous and compactly supported, |g₁| ≤ 1, and |g₁ − β| = |π(g) − π(β)| ≤ |g − β| μ-a.e. on K.
- With a standard mollifier φ_δ ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, put g₂ := g₁ * φ_δ (coefficientwise). Then g₂ is C^∞, and |g₂(x)| ≤ ∫ |g₁(x − y)| φ_δ(y) dy ≤ 1 because |·| is a norm. Also g₂ → g₁ uniformly as δ ↓ 0 because g₁ is uniformly continuous; fix δ with sup |g₂ − g₁| ≤ ε/(μ(K) + 1).
- Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K and spt χ ⊆ V (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χ g₂.
Then ω is smooth with compact support, spt ω ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, and |ω| = χ|g₂| ≤ 1. So ω is admissible for M_W(T).

5. Estimate. We have ω = g₂ on K and ω = 0 off V. By step 1, μ-a.e. |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1. As μ = θH^n⌞M:
T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ = ∫_K ⟨g₂, ξ⟩ dμ + ∫_{V∖K} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ
≥ ∫_K ⟨β, ξ⟩ dμ − ∫_K |g₂ − β| dμ − μ(V ∖ K)
≥ μ(K) − (∫_K |g₂ − g₁| dμ + ∫_K |g₁ − β| dμ) − ε
> μ(K) − 3ε > λ.

6. Conclusion. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) > λ for every real λ ∈ [0, μ(W)). So M_W(T) ≥ μ(W), and with step 2, M_W(T) = μ(W). If n > P, then H^n = 0 on ℝ^P, so μ = 0, T = 0 and both sides vanish; step 3 is then vacuous.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: |α(τ₁,…,τ_n)| ≤ |α| for orthonormal τ, and J(ξ) is a unit covector with ⟨J(ξ), ξ⟩ = 1.
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n from the integral formula.
Lower bound: inner and outer regularity, L¹-density of continuous maps, radial retraction, mollification and a cut-off give an admissible ω with T(ω) > μ(K) − 3ε > λ.

subproblems.title: The mass density of an integer multiplicity current equals its multiplicity almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep with R.Represents T), with weight μ_T = R.measure = θH^n⌞M. Then HasMassDensity T x θ(x) holds for μ_T-a.e. x. That is, θ(x) ≥ 0 and M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, where B_ρ(x) is the open ball and ω_n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, p. 91 (chapter-04.txt line 350: Θ^n(V, x) = θ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, by Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)). This is Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1)–(2) with Theorem 1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298–325), the fact used in step 2 of the parent proof. The argument uses two ingredients:
- the approximate tangent planes supplied by R (Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and Remark 1.5(3), lines 77–101);
- the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for Radon measures (Ch. 1, Corollary 3.17 with Remark 3.11(3), chapter-01.txt lines 773–960), which is the content of Remark 1.8(1).

Notation: H^n = μHE[n], μ := H^n⌞M, ν := R.measure = θμ, ω_n := unitBallVolume n; B_ρ(x) is the open ball and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball.

1. Local finiteness. For compact K ⊆ U: μ(K) = H^n(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M), and ν(K) < ∞.

2. Unweighted density (Remark 1.5(3)). By the axiom orients of R, for μ-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. That is, ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as ρ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,ρ}(y) = ρ^{−1}(y − x).
Fix such an x ∈ M ⊆ U, s > 0 with B̄_s(x) ⊆ U, and 0 < ε < 1. Choose f₁, f₂ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with:
- f₁ = 1 on B̄_{1−ε}(0) and spt f₁ ⊆ B_1(0);
- f₂ = 1 on B̄_1(0) and spt f₂ ⊆ B_{1+ε}(0).
H^n is translation invariant and H^n(ρ^{−1}A) = ρ^{−n}H^n(A) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Also η_{x,ρ}(M) ∩ B_t(0) = η_{x,ρ}(M ∩ B_{tρ}(x)). Hence for 0 < ρ < s/2:
∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f₁ dH^n ≤ ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ρ^{−n}μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f₂ dH^n,
all finite by step 1. H^n⌞Q is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure carried by a linear isometry ℝ^n ≅ Q (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). So ∫_Q f₁ dH^n ≥ H^n(Q ∩ B̄_{1−ε}(0)) = ω_n(1 − ε)^n and ∫_Q f₂ dH^n ≤ H^n(Q ∩ B_{1+ε}(0)) = ω_n(1 + ε)^n.
Letting ρ ↓ 0 and then ε ↓ 0 gives μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1 and μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1. In particular μ(B̄_ρ(x)) > 0 for small ρ > 0.
Edge cases: for n = 0, Q = {0}, H^0 is counting measure, ω_0 = 1 and ρ^0 = 1, and the same computation applies. If n > P, then H^n = 0 on ℝ^P, ν = 0 and the statement is vacuous.

3. Lebesgue differentiation.
- Let K_j := {y : |y| ≤ j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}. Each K_j is a compact subset of U whose interior contains {y : |y| < j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/j}, so U = ⋃_j int K_j.
- The measures μ_j := μ⌞K_j and ν_j := ν⌞K_j = θμ_j are finite (step 1), and dν_j/dμ_j = θ μ_j-a.e.
- By the Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Ch. 1, 3.17 with 3.11(3); Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv) there is Z_j with μ_j(Z_j) = 0, i.e. μ(Z_j ∩ K_j) = 0, such that ν_j(B̄_ρ(x))/μ_j(B̄_ρ(x)) → θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0 for every x ∉ Z_j.
- Let E := ⋃_j (Z_j ∩ K_j) ∪ E₂, where E₂ is the μ-null exceptional set of step 2. Then μ(E) = 0.
- Let x ∈ M ∖ E and choose j with x ∈ int K_j; then x ∉ Z_j. For 0 < ρ < dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ int K_j) we have B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K_j, so μ_j(B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and ν_j(B̄_ρ(x)) = ν(B̄_ρ(x)).
Hence ν(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) = [ν(B̄_ρ(x))/μ(B̄_ρ(x))]·[μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n)] → θ(x)·1 = θ(x).

4. Open balls. For x ∈ M ∖ E and 0 < t < 1, ν(B̄_{tρ}(x)) ≤ ν(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ν(B̄_ρ(x)). Hence liminf_{ρ↓0} ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) ≥ t^nθ(x) and limsup_{ρ↓0} ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) ≤ θ(x). Letting t ↑ 1, ν(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x).

Thus M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) in [0, ∞] (with ω_nρ^n ∈ (0, ∞)), and θ(x) ≥ 0. This is HasMassDensity T x θ(x).

6. Conclusion. The set where the conclusion fails is contained in E ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ M). Since ν ≪ μ, ν(E) = 0, and ν(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0. Hence HasMassDensity T x θ(x) for ν-a.e. x.

Let ν be any measure on ℝ^N = Euclid N with its Borel σ-algebra, O ⊆ ℝ^N an open set, and A ⊆ O. The comparison is applied to the outer measure of ν. A positive normalization constant replaces 1, which the parent's note allows. - **(L1)** ω := Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume (n : ℝ) satisfies 0 < ω < ∞, by `realUnitBallVolume_pos (Nat.cast_nonneg n)` and `realUnitBallVolume_ne_top`.
- **(L2)** s := Chapter02.simonAreaNormalization n satisfies 0 < s < ∞, by `simonAreaNormalization_pos` and `simonAreaNormalization_ne_top`.
  - Simon's Hausdorff measure on E satisfies Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) = s • μHE[n], by `simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure`.
  - Its outer measure is Chapter01.simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n : ℝ), by `simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure` with 0 ≤ (n : ℝ).
- **(L3)** For an outer measure μ' on E, a set A₂ and x ∈ E, the upper density is Θ*ⁿ(μ', A₂, x) = limsup over r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0) of μ'(A₂ ∩ B̄_r(x)) / (ω · ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ)). In Lean these are `Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity` and `dimensionalDensityQuotient`.
- **(L4)** Simon 3.3 (`Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3`): let μ' be a Borel regular outer measure on a metric space, 0 ≤ n, A₁ ⊆ A₂ and t ≥ 0 real. If ofReal t ≤ Θ*ⁿ(μ', A₂, x) for every x ∈ A₁, then ofReal t · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (A₁) ≤ μ'(A₂).
- **(L5)** For any measure ν on the Borel space E, the outer measure μ' := ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular (`Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular`) and agrees with ν on every set.

**Proof.**

1. **The constant.** Put τ := c / ω.toReal. By (L1), ω.toReal > 0, so τ > 0 and ofReal τ > 0. Define C := (ofReal τ · s)⁻¹. By (L2) and ofReal τ > 0, the product ofReal τ · s is nonzero, so C ≠ ∞. C depends only on n and c.

2. **Setup.** Fix ν, A and O as in the statement and let μ' := ν.toOuterMeasure, which is Borel regular by (L5).

3. **Density lower bound.** Let x ∈ A and take t₀ > 0 from the hypothesis. O is open and x ∈ A ⊆ O, so there is ρ > 0 with B(x, ρ) ⊆ O. Let r ∈ (0, min(t₀, ρ)).
   - (a) B̄_r(x) ⊆ B(x, ρ) ⊆ O, hence O ∩ B̄_r(x) = B̄_r(x).
   - (b) ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(r)^n = ofReal(rⁿ), by `ENNReal.rpow_natCast` and `ENNReal.ofReal_pow` with r ≥ 0. Also rⁿ > 0, so 0 < ω · ofReal(rⁿ) < ∞.
   - (c) Since ω ≠ ∞ we have ω = ofReal(ω.toReal), and τ · ω.toReal = c. So ofReal(τ) · (ω · ofReal(rⁿ)) = ofReal(τ · ω.toReal · rⁿ) = ofReal(c rⁿ) ≤ ν(B̄_r(x)), by the hypothesis at t = r ∈ (0, t₀).
   - (d) The density quotient at radius r is μ'(O ∩ B̄_r(x)) / (ω · ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ)) = ν(B̄_r(x)) / (ω · ofReal(rⁿ)). By (c) and the ENNReal rule a ≤ b/d ⇔ a·d ≤ b for 0 < d < ∞ (`ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le`), this quotient is ≥ ofReal τ.
   - (e) The interval (0, min(t₀, ρ)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, so the inequality holds eventually, hence frequently, since 𝓝[>] 0 is nontrivial. Therefore Θ*ⁿ(μ', O, x) = limsup of the quotient ≥ ofReal τ (`Filter.le_limsup_of_frequently_le`; the coboundedness side condition is automatic in [0, ∞]).

   So ofReal τ ≤ Θ*ⁿ(μ', O, x) for every x ∈ A.

4. **Comparison.** Apply (L4) with μ', n := (n : ℝ) ≥ 0, A₁ := A, A₂ := O (A ⊆ O) and t := τ ≥ 0. This gives ofReal τ · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n : ℝ) (A) ≤ μ'(O) = ν(O).

5. **Normalization.** By (L2), simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n : ℝ) (A) = simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) (A) = s · μHE[n](A). Hence (ofReal τ · s) · μHE[n](A) ≤ ν(O).

6. **Division.** Since 0 < ofReal τ · s < ∞, step 5 is equivalent to μHE[n](A) ≤ ν(O) / (ofReal τ · s) = (ofReal τ · s)⁻¹ · ν(O) = C · ν(O), by `ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le` and `ENNReal.div_eq_inv_mul`. This is the claim, with the finite constant C from step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Let ω = realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞) and s = simonAreaNormalization n ∈ (0, ∞). Set τ := c/ω.toReal > 0 and C := (ofReal τ · s)⁻¹, which is finite.
For x ∈ A, small closed balls B̄_r(x) lie in the open set O. The bound ν(B̄_r(x)) ≥ c rⁿ makes every small-radius density quotient ≥ τ, so Θ*ⁿ(ν, O, x) ≥ τ.
simon_theorem_3_3, applied to the Borel regular outer measure of ν with A₁ = A and A₂ = O, gives τ · H_S^n(A) ≤ ν(O).
Since H_S^n = s · μHE[n], dividing by the positive finite number τ·s gives μHE[n](A) ≤ C · ν(O).

Accepted proof:
**Source:** step 3 of the parent proof (localized outer regularity). The parent's exhaustion of W by sets V_j is replaced by a countable cover of A by open balls of finite μ-measure; this is the same argument. Notation: E := ℝ^N = Euclid N, B(x, r) is the open ball, and N, μ, A are as in the statement. Fix ε ∈ (0, ∞], so ε ≠ 0.

1. **Choice of radii.** For each x ∈ A choose r(x) > 0 with μ(B(x, r(x))) < ∞. This uses the hypothesis and choice; in Lean, `choose! r hr hfin using hloc`.

2. **Countable subcover.** The sets B(x, r(x)), x ∈ A, are open, and E is second countable. By the Lindelöf property (Lean: `TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable` for the family indexed by the subtype of A) there is a countable T ⊆ A with ⋃_{i∈T} B(i, r(i)) = ⋃_{x∈A} B(x, r(x)). Write B_i := B(i, r(i)) for i ∈ T. Each x ∈ A lies in its own ball B(x, r(x)) because r(x) > 0. Hence A ⊆ ⋃_{x∈A} B(x, r(x)) = ⋃_{i∈T} B_i.

3. **Error budget.** T is countable and ε ≠ 0, so there are real numbers ε_i > 0 (i ∈ T) with Σ_{i∈T} ε_i < ε. In Lean: `ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable` applied to the countable type T.

4. **Local approximation.** Fix i ∈ T and let μ_i := μ⌞B_i (Lean `μ.restrict B_i`).
   - (a) μ_i(E) = μ(B_i) < ∞ by step 1. So μ_i is a finite Borel measure on the metric space E, hence outer regular. In Mathlib, `Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure` gives weak regularity, and weakly regular measures are outer regular.
   - (b) The restriction satisfies μ_i ≤ μ setwise (`Measure.restrict_le_self`). Hence μ_i(A ∩ B_i) ≤ μ_i(A) ≤ μ(A) = 0 < ε_i.
   - (c) By outer regularity (`Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt` applied to the set A ∩ B_i and the bound ε_i) there is an open O_i ⊇ A ∩ B_i with μ_i(O_i) < ε_i.
   - (d) O_i is open, hence measurable, so μ_i(O_i) = μ(O_i ∩ B_i) (`Measure.restrict_apply`). Thus μ(O_i ∩ B_i) < ε_i.

5. **Definition of O.** Put O := ⋃_{i∈T} (O_i ∩ B_i). Each O_i ∩ B_i is an intersection of two open sets, hence open, so O is open.

6. **A ⊆ O.** Let x ∈ A. By step 2 there is i ∈ T with x ∈ B_i. Then x ∈ A ∩ B_i ⊆ O_i, so x ∈ O_i ∩ B_i ⊆ O.

7. **Measure bound.** By countable subadditivity (`measure_iUnion_le`), then step 4(d) termwise (`ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum`), then step 3: μ(O) ≤ Σ_{i∈T} μ(O_i ∩ B_i) ≤ Σ_{i∈T} ε_i < ε. If A = ∅, the same computation applies: T may be empty, O = ∅ and μ(O) = 0 < ε.

8. **Conclusion.** O is open, A ⊆ O and μ(O) < ε, as required. ∎
proof_key_steps: Around each x ∈ A choose an open ball B(x, r(x)) of finite μ-measure.
Second countability (Lindelöf) gives a countable subfamily (B_i)_{i∈T} whose union contains A.
Choose positive budgets ε_i with Σ_{i∈T} ε_i < ε.
The finite measure μ⌞B_i is outer regular. Since μ⌞B_i(A ∩ B_i) = 0, there is an open O_i ⊇ A ∩ B_i with μ(O_i ∩ B_i) < ε_i.
O := ⋃_i (O_i ∩ B_i) is open and contains A, and subadditivity gives μ(O) ≤ Σ ε_i < ε.

Source: parent step 1 ("Scaling of H^n … (1.1) ∫_{S(M)} F dH^n = λ^{-n} ∫_M F(S(y)) dH^n(y), using the change of variables formula for the measurable embedding S (Mathlib integral_map_equiv / lintegral_map_equiv) and linearity in the measure"), stated for c = λ and T := S^{-1}, so that T^{-1}(M) = S(M) = c^{-1}M and F(z) = g(cz).

1. T is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P (its inverse is x ↦ c^{-1}x), hence a measurable embedding for the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Mathlib: (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero c hc).measurableEmbedding); in particular T is measurable and injective.

2. Push-forward of H^n by T. Let B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then (T_#H^n)(B) = H^n(T^{-1}(B)) (Measure.map_apply, T measurable, B measurable), and T^{-1}(B) = {x : cx ∈ B} = c^{-1}B := {c^{-1}b : b ∈ B} (Set.preimage_smul₀). The scaling law of Hausdorff measure holds for every set S and every r ≠ 0: H^n(rS) = ‖r‖₊^n · H^n(S) (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). With r = c^{-1}: H^n(c^{-1}B) = ‖c^{-1}‖₊^n · H^n(B). Since c^{-1} > 0 we have ‖c^{-1}‖₊ = c^{-1} as a nonnegative real, so the factor ‖c^{-1}‖₊^n, viewed in [0,∞], equals ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) (c^{-n} ≥ 0). Hence (T_#H^n)(B) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n(B) for every Borel B, and since two measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal, T_#H^n = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n.

3. Proof of (i). For a measurable embedding T, a measure ν and an arbitrary set M (no measurability of M is needed), (T_#ν)⌞M = T_#(ν⌞T^{-1}(M)) (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). With ν = H^n and step 2:
 T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}(M)) = (T_#H^n)⌞M = (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n)⌞M = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · (H^n⌞M)
 (restriction commutes with scalar multiplication of the measure, Measure.restrict_smul).

4. Proof of (ii). For a measurable embedding T, a measure ν and every function g : ℝ^P → [0,∞] (measurable or not), ∫⁻ g d(T_#ν) = ∫⁻ (g ∘ T) dν (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). Take ν = H^n⌞T^{-1}(M). Then
 ∫⁻_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = ∫⁻ g d(T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}(M))) = ∫⁻ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n⌞M) = ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · ∫⁻_M g dH^n,
 by (i) and the linearity of the lower integral in the measure, ∫⁻ g d(a·μ) = a · ∫⁻ g dμ (lintegral_smul_measure).

5. Proof of (iii). For a measurable embedding T, a measure ν and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ g d(T_#ν) = ∫ (g ∘ T) dν (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; no integrability assumption is needed: g is T_#ν-integrable iff g ∘ T is ν-integrable, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise). With ν = H^n⌞T^{-1}(M), (i), and ∫ g d(a·μ) = a.toReal · ∫ g dμ for a ∈ [0,∞] (integral_smul_measure):
 ∫_{T^{-1}(M)} g(cz) dH^n(z) = ∫ g d(ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n}) · H^n⌞M) = (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n})).toReal · ∫_M g dH^n = c^{-n} · ∫_M g dH^n,
 because c^{-n} ≥ 0 gives (ENNReal.ofReal(c^{-n})).toReal = c^{-n} (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). This completes the proof of (i), (ii) and (iii).

T^{-1}(B) = c^{-1}B and the Hausdorff scaling law H^n(c^{-1}B) = c^{-n}H^n(B) give T_#H^n = c^{-n}H^n.
Restriction along the measurable embedding: T_#(H^n⌞T^{-1}M) = (T_#H^n)⌞M = c^{-n}H^n⌞M (proves (i)).
Change of variables for lower and Bochner integrals over T_#ν, plus linearity in the measure, give (ii) and (iii).
